scope.method: targeted narrative review of primary abstracts and user requirements; not a systematic literature review
limitations: Publisher abstracts rather than full texts were used for some studies.
Source URLs and access date are recorded; original external page bytes were not snapshotted.
Host activation and runtime effectiveness are not evaluated in this creation run.

findings.claim: People can substantially overestimate mechanistic explanatory understanding.
findings.rationale: Human cognitive study; use only to motivate explicit gap detection, not to assert agent effect.

findings.claim: Self-generated explanations in physics learning were associated with deeper principle-oriented learning.
findings.rationale: Transfer to code reasoning is a design hypothesis, not an established effect in code agents.

findings.claim: Programmers in maintenance tasks seek and relate information and ask diverse cross-code questions.
findings.rationale: Supports scoped cross-file question-driven traversal over component summaries.

findings.claim: Reachability questions occur frequently and can be difficult in software development tasks.
findings.rationale: Supports checking alternate paths and constraining negative claims.

findings.claim: A 42-student functional-testing experiment found more confirmatory than disconfirmatory cases; time-pressure effect was not supported.
findings.rationale: Qualify population and avoid implying time pressure causes confirmation bias.

findings.claim: Mechanistic policy explanations reliably reduce political extremity in general.
findings.rationale: 2013 source suggested an effect but 2021 preregistered replications failed to support general moderation; no technical transfer.

findings.claim: Preregistered policy-explanation replications found reduced perceived understanding but not the original moderation outcome.
findings.rationale: Use as a transfer and epistemic-certainty warning.

findings.claim: Provenance can explicitly represent entities, activities, agents and their relations.
findings.rationale: Skill uses lightweight source/claim IDs, not PROV-O/RDF conformance.

findings.claim: The user requests a reusable approach to development and understanding of existing execution flows.
findings.rationale: Own bounded causal comprehension, with modes and concise representation.

findings.claim: The requested package must be multi-host, description <=500 characters, and Top-100 self-sufficient; specialist practices include versioning and traceability.
findings.rationale: These are explicit user requirements plus governing creation-skill versioning contract.

requirements.statement: Require mechanistic input->guard->transition->effect explanation with gap identification.
Traverse question-relevant cross-file/control/data/event/state relationships and cite sources.
Constrain exhaustive reachability and negative claims to proved, enumerated closed-world scope.
Actively seek discriminating disconfirming paths and document checks.
Avoid projecting psychological experimental effects into assured engineering gains; label inference and contradictory evidence.
Give material claims source IDs and statuses; supply optional typed output and validator.
Deliver host-neutral SKILL first-100 complete, <=500 metadata, SemVer/changelog, direct references and explicit fallback.
Bound scope to understanding/challenge/proposed impact and hand off unrelated implementation/debugging/diagram work.
Provide concise explanatory report with evidence, alternatives, unknowns and next verification.
Provide proportionate static evaluation assets and research-to-skill change accounting without unsupported runtime claims.
